chunks: Ali ibn Isma'il narrated from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) about a man who had illicit sexual intercourse with a woman: Does he marry her mother from wet-nursing or her daughter? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: One of the two Imams (referring to Imam al-Sadiq or Imam al-Kazim)
key_terms.الرِّضَاعَةِ: Wet-nursing (creating kinship ties for marriage prohibition)
key_terms.فَجَرَ: To commit illicit sexual intercourse (zina) or fornication

ai.seo_question: Does illicit sex create a permanent marriage prohibition with the woman's mother or daughter?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that illicit sexual intercourse (*fujur*) establishes a permanent marital prohibition (*mahramiyyah*) akin to lineage, specifically barring marriage to the woman’s mother or daughter. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that *fujur* creates a real bond of affinity, preventing marriage not only to the direct female line but also extending through wet-nursing connections, thereby preserving family integrity and preventing confusion of lineage.
